items.title: Bayes-reversed transition kernels for a diffusion
items.strategy: Define the reverse-time kernel from the forward marginal density and transition density, retaining positivity, normalization, Chapman–Kolmogorov and regularity as explicit hypotheses to be checked by the consumer lemma.

items.title: Quadratic variation of a continuous local martingale
items.strategy: Use everywhere-continuous adapted input representatives for stopping; localize to bounded martingales, prove the common-refinement L2 Cauchy bound for correctly indexed coefficients, and pass the square identity to the compatible bracket limits and product formula.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Each input local martingale below is taken with everywhere-continuous adapted paths; it suffices that its full continuity event belongs to the initial sigma-algebra, so it can first be normalized there. All pathwise stopping operations use these representatives. Let $M$ be a real continuous local martingale on $[0,T]$ with $M_0=0$, where a local martingale means that some increasing stopping times tending to $T$ make the stopped processes martingales. Then there is a unique continuous increasing process $[M]$ with $[M]_0=0$ such that the step-endpoint and partial-increment sums of squared increments along every deterministic partition sequence whose mesh tends to zero converge uniformly in probability to $[M]$. Moreover $M_t^2-[M]_t$ is a continuous local martingale. For a continuous $d$-dimensional local martingale $M$ started at zero, polarization defines continuous covariations $[M^i,M^j]$ with $M^iM^j-[M^i,M^j]$ local martingales. More generally, if $X=M+A$ and $Z=N+C$ with continuous local martingales $M,N$ and continuous finite-variation processes $A,C$, then left-step sums define the localized integrals against $M,N$ and
$$X_tZ_t-X_0Z_0=\int_0^t X_s\,dZ_s+\int_0^t Z_s\,dX_s+[M,N]_t,$$
where finite-variation integrals are pathwise Lebesgue–Stieltjes integrals and local-martingale integrals are the limits of the displayed left-step sums. Stopping a continuous local martingale at a bounded stopping time preserves its local-martingale property; if the stopped process is bounded, it is a true martingale. A continuous finite-variation local martingale is constant.

items.title: A translated conditional density factorizes after subtraction
items.strategy: Apply Lebesgue change of variables to the joint density under the determinant-one shear; use completed-product agreement and Tonelli only on the separated factors, with Countable Choice explicit.

items.title: An elliptic local martingale has a Brownian driver
items.strategy: Construct the inverse-diffusion stochastic integral by stopped left-step sums, prove its martingale isometry and covariation from the defining product-martingale identities, then apply the vector Lévy characterization.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a continuous adapted $d$-dimensional local martingale with $M_0=0$. Let $(\sigma_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a continuous adapted process of invertible $d\times d$ matrices such that $\|\sigma_t^{-1}\|\le C$ for a deterministic finite constant $C$, and suppose every entry of $\sigma$ is locally square-integrable in time almost surely. Write $[M^i,M^j]$ for the continuous bracket characterized by the local-martingale property of $M^iM^j-[M^i,M^j]$, and assume
$$[M^i,M^j]_t=\int_0^t(\sigma_s\sigma_s^{\mathsf T})_{ij}\,ds\qquad(1\le i,j\le d).$$
Then the stochastic integral $B_t=\int_0^t\sigma_s^{-1}\,dM_s$, constructed as the localized $L^2$ limit of left-step sums, has a continuous version with $[B^i,B^j]_t=\delta_{ij}t$. Consequently $B$ is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to the given filtration.

items.title: A normalized parabolic Bellman equation has a bounded weak solution
items.strategy: Construct a discounted positive finite-difference fixed point, preserve Lipschitz and semiconvex bounds, obtain bounded weak derivatives by test duality, and prove exact Bellman equality through quadratic contacts.

items.title: A parabolic Bellman barrier with a Lebesgue height bound
items.strategy: Use explicit comparison functions for decay and future cutoff; prove determinant-cofactor integration identities and a fixed-exponent height estimate, then pass the mollified limit with an exponential majorant.

items.title: Stopped occupation absolute continuity for uniformly elliptic Ito processes
items.strategy: Smooth all constant-matrix barrier inequalities before stochastic evaluation, apply a stopped discounted Ito estimate, and transfer weighted nullness through a strictly positive determinant weight.

items.title: Forward density duality identifies an auxiliary reverse process
items.strategy: Use positive harmonic kernel mixtures and complementary conservation, transfer time-averaged forward convergence through occupation absolute continuity, identify marginals before endpoint conditional limits, and compare continuous path laws.

items.title: Forward Kolmogorov duality gives reversed martingales
items.strategy: Differentiate the finite-time forward density/test product under explicit backward-Kolmogorov and local-flux hypotheses, then extend conditioning tests to the reversed natural filtration.

items.title: Reversed kernels, generator, and martingale problem
items.strategy: Prove Bayes kernels and formal adjoint algebra unconditionally; obtain the martingale assertion only under the explicitly stated forward transition-duality and local weighted-flux hypotheses, proved by the new local forward-duality helper.

items.title: Anderson's bounded-start reverse-time diffusion theorem
items.strategy: Use the augmented joint Fokker–Planck equation to identify a product Gaussian density, repeat the factorization conditionally to prove reverse-noise increments and their filtration properties, and convert the forward Itô integral to a backward Itô integral with its covariation correction.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $t_0<T$, integers $d,r\ge1$, and a filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t_0\le t\le T},P)$ satisfying the usual conditions. Let $W$ be an adapted standard $r$-dimensional Brownian motion such that $W_t-W_s$ is independent of $\mathcal F_s$ and has law $N_r(0,(t-s)I_r)$ for every $t_0\le s<t\le T$. Let $X_{t_0}$ be $\mathcal F_{t_0}$-measurable, almost surely bounded, and independent of the future Brownian increments $\sigma(W_t-W_{t_0}:t_0\le t\le T)$. Let
$$dX_t=b(X_t,t)\,dt+\sigma(X_t,t)\,dW_t,\qquad X_t\in\mathbb R^d,$$
for $t\in[t_0,T]$. Assume the drift and diffusion path integrals satisfy $\int_{t_0}^T|b(X_s,s)|ds<\infty$ and $\int_{t_0}^T\|\sigma(X_s,s)\|_F^2ds<\infty$ almost surely, and that this SDE has a unique nonexplosive strong solution. Put $a=\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T}$. Also assume the strong restart property: for each deterministic $s\in[t_0,T]$, the future path $(X_r)_{s\le r\le T}$ is almost surely a measurable function of $X_s$ and $(W_r-W_s)_{s\le r\le T}$. Assume the coefficients and densities are smooth enough for the displayed derivatives and Itô identities to hold. Assume the marginal density $p_t(x)$ is positive wherever used and is a unique smooth solution of
$$\partial_t p_t=L_t^*p_t,\qquad L_t^*r=-\sum_i\partial_i(b_i r)+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\partial_i\partial_j(a_{ij}r).$$
Define the $r$-vector process $\widetilde W$ by $\widetilde W_{t_0}=0$ and
$$d\widetilde W_t^k=dW_t^k+c_k(X_t,t)\,dt,\qquad c_k(x,t)=p_t(x)^{-1}\sum_i\partial_i\!\left(p_t(x)\sigma_{ik}(x,t)\right).$$
Assume the augmented process $(X,\widetilde W)$ has a unique smooth joint density solving its augmented forward Kolmogorov equation for $t>t_0$, and for every $t>s\ge t_0$ its conditional joint density given $\widetilde W_s$ is the unique smooth solution of the corresponding conditional augmented equation; all displayed derivatives and density integrals are valid. Then the following hold.

1. For $t>s\ge t_0$, $X_t$ is independent of $\widetilde W_t-\widetilde W_s$, and this increment has law $N_r(0,(t-s)I_r)$.
2. Put $U=T-t_0$, $Y_u=X_{T-u}$, and $B_u=\widetilde W_{T-u}-\widetilde W_T$ for $0\le u\le U$. With $\mathcal G_u=\sigma(Y_v,B_v:0\le v\le u)$, $B$ is a standard $r$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to $(\mathcal G_u)$.
3. In the backward Itô convention, $Y$ satisfies
$$dY_u=\left[-b(Y_u,T-u)+(\nabla\!\cdot a)(Y_u,T-u)+a(Y_u,T-u)\nabla\log p_{T-u}(Y_u)\right]du+\sigma(Y_u,T-u)\,dB_u,$$
where $(\nabla\!\cdot a)_i=\sum_j\partial_j a_{ij}$. The score is asserted only where $p_{T-u}>0$; no density or score regularity beyond the stated hypotheses is implied.

items.title: Bayes-reversed Gaussian smoothing kernels
items.strategy: Define the reversed kernel from the explicit Gaussian marginal and transition densities, verify its normalization by the forward marginal identity, and verify reverse Chapman–Kolmogorov by Gaussian transition composition.

items.title: Brownian reconstruction with a predictable elliptic coefficient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a finite horizon $T>0$ and a filtration $(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}$. Let $M$ be a continuous adapted $d$-dimensional local martingale with $M_0=0$. Let $\sigma$ be a predictable process of invertible $d\times d$ matrices, with $\|\sigma_t^{-1}\|\le C$ for a finite deterministic constant $C$ and $\int_0^T\|\sigma_t\|_F^2dt<\infty$ almost surely. Suppose
$$[M^i,M^j]_t=\int_0^t(\sigma_s\sigma_s^{\mathsf T})_{ij}ds.$$
Then predictable elementary sums, completed in the localized bracket-energy norm, define $B=\int\sigma^{-1}dM$. It has an adapted continuous version, is standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion in the given filtration, and
$$M_t=\int_0^t\sigma_s\,dB_s$$
up to indistinguishability. The integral on the right is the localized predictable Brownian integral defined by elementary sums and their $L^2$ completion. This construction on the given finite horizon does not require completeness or right continuity of the filtration, and no continuity of $\sigma$ is assumed.

items.title: Reverse-time SDE for an unbounded-start Markov diffusion
items.strategy: Use assumed reverse martingale-problem existence and uniform ellipticity to construct an auxiliary Ito process; derive stopped occupation absolute continuity with a locally proved Bellman barrier, identify its Bayes law by positive forward-density mixtures and time averaging, then retain the original predictable Brownian reconstruction and uniqueness proof.

items.title: Generator and martingale problem for reversed Gaussian smoothing
items.strategy: Differentiate the explicit Gaussian reverse-kernel expression on compactly supported tests, use the heat equation, expand the adjoint product rule to expose the plus-score sign, and integrate the transition identity to obtain the localized martingale problem.

items.title: Reverse Gaussian smoothing on a truncated time interval
items.strategy: Use the reversed-kernel martingale problem, localize coordinate and product tests, reconstruct Brownian motion by the inverse scalar diffusion and the vector Lévy characterization, apply the published Lipschitz SDE well-posedness interface on [0,T−epsilon], and carry the separate endpoint coupling bound with no score claim at zero.

items.title: State-dependent diffusion needs a divergence correction
items.strategy: Transform Brownian motion by a smooth increasing diffeomorphism with nonconstant derivative, compute its forward score and diffusion-matrix divergence, and show the score-only reverse drift differs from the proven generator formula.

items.title: Bounded-start Brownian reversal under Anderson's hypotheses
items.strategy: Specialize Anderson's theorem to scalar Brownian motion with a bounded smooth initial density, substitute the explicit Gaussian convolution for the marginal density, and retain the joint-density uniqueness premise explicitly.

items.title: A stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck diffusion reverses to itself
items.strategy: Insert the stationary Gaussian score into the general reversal formula, compute the reversed drift, and verify the centered normal law remains invariant by the explicit transition mean and variance.
